# Turing Pi 2 BMC firmware (excavador-turing fork)

> A maintained fork of the Turing Pi 2 BMC firmware — the management computer on a Turing Pi 2 cluster board, which powers, flashes and consoles the four compute modules. Upstream's last release is v2.1.0 (February 2025) and its update mirror stops earlier still. This fork adds an update that takes itself back when the board does not come up right, VLANs on the board's own switch, a certificate a browser accepts, the board's own address from the interface, and metrics where there were none. Everything on this site was measured on real boards; every page says where and when.

Generated by `scripts/llms.py` from the site's own navigation and each page's description. Do not edit.

## Home

- [Home](https://turingpi.xyz/): A maintained fork of the Turing Pi 2 BMC firmware: updates that take themselves back, VLANs on the board's own switch, a certificate that does not rot.

## Features

- [Overview](https://turingpi.xyz/features/): What this firmware does that the stock Turing Pi 2 BMC does not, one page per feature, each with the measurements behind the claim.
- [One page over every board](https://turingpi.xyz/features/one-page-over-every-board/): Drive every Turing Pi 2 in the cluster from one page that holds no credential of its own and never exposes a board to the network.
- [Fresh, and fixed](https://turingpi.xyz/features/fresh-and-fixed/): A longterm kernel and a supported Buildroot under the Turing Pi 2 BMC, with named faults from the stock firmware taken out.
- [Update without touching your nodes](https://turingpi.xyz/features/update-without-touching-your-nodes/): Update the Turing Pi 2 BMC while the four compute modules stay powered and running, measured across every flash on these boards.
- [Updates that undo themselves](https://turingpi.xyz/features/updates-that-undo-themselves/): A new BMC image boots on trial and is kept only when the board answers properly afterwards, so a bad flash undoes itself without a trip to the rack.
- [See what the board sees](https://turingpi.xyz/features/see-what-the-board-sees/): The Turing Pi 2 board temperature, the fan step and the trip that explains it, plus every reading the stock firmware never described.
- [Pick a version, from anywhere](https://turingpi.xyz/features/pick-a-version/): Install firmware from this fork, from upstream or from the SD card, every candidate checksum-verified and compared by version rather than by name.
- [A console to every module](https://turingpi.xyz/features/a-console-to-every-module/): A serial console to each of the four compute modules in the browser, replaying the boot output you were not there to watch.
- [A certificate that does not rot](https://turingpi.xyz/features/a-certificate-that-does-not-rot/): The BMC issues its own HTTPS certificate with a name your browser accepts, renews it before it expires, and never overwrites one you installed.
- [The board describes its own API](https://turingpi.xyz/features/the-board-describes-itself/): The BMC serves its own OpenAPI 3.1 document, so the API reference on this site is generated from the board rather than written by hand.
- [Flash a module from the card](https://turingpi.xyz/features/flash-from-the-card/): Write a node image to a compute module straight from the board's own SD card, with the board saying which files can be written and why the rest cannot.
- [Who may reach this board](https://turingpi.xyz/features/who-may-reach-this-board/): The BMC password and the trusted proxy that may speak for a user, both readable and both changeable from the page that asks you for one.
- [The arguments: One page over every board](https://turingpi.xyz/why/one-page-over-every-board/): Why one page over every board holds no credential of its own, and what that rules out for the fleet interface.
- [The arguments: Fresh, and fixed](https://turingpi.xyz/why/fresh-and-fixed/): Why this firmware moved to a longterm kernel and a supported Buildroot, and the named faults that came out with it.
- [The arguments: Update without touching your nodes](https://turingpi.xyz/why/update-without-touching-your-nodes/): Why a BMC update leaves the compute modules powered, and the measurements taken across every flash on these boards.
- [The arguments: Updates that undo themselves](https://turingpi.xyz/why/updates-that-undo-themselves/): Why a new image boots on trial, what promoting on boot alone cost upstream's users, and what the gate has recorded since.
- [The arguments: See what the board sees](https://turingpi.xyz/why/see-what-the-board-sees/): Why the board's temperature and fan readings belong together, and what upstream's firmware never described.
- [The arguments: Pick a version, from anywhere](https://turingpi.xyz/why/pick-a-version/): Why firmware candidates are compared numerically and checksum-verified, and what comparing them by name used to do.
- [The arguments: A console to every module](https://turingpi.xyz/why/a-console-to-every-module/): Why a serial console in the browser needs a replayed scrollback, what it costs, and how the fork's console was proved.
- [The arguments: A certificate that does not rot](https://turingpi.xyz/why/a-certificate-that-does-not-rot/): Why the BMC issues and renews its own certificate, what upstream's did instead, and the measurements behind both.
- [The arguments: The board describes its own API](https://turingpi.xyz/why/the-board-describes-itself/): Why the API reference is generated from the board's own OpenAPI document rather than written and kept by hand.
- [The arguments: Flash a module from the card](https://turingpi.xyz/why/flash-from-the-card/): Why the board decides which SD-card files can be written to a module, and what the two flash bugs behind this were.
- [The arguments: Who may reach this board](https://turingpi.xyz/why/who-may-reach-this-board/): Why the password and the trusted proxy are both shown on the page that asks for one, and what a hidden default costs.

## Docs

- [Overview](https://turingpi.xyz/guides/): Every guide and reference for this Turing Pi 2 BMC firmware: install it, upgrade from stock, recover a bad flash, segment the network, monitor it.
- [Guides: Install](https://turingpi.xyz/guides/install/): Install this firmware on your own Turing Pi 2: which file to take, flashing over the network or from the SD card, and what to check afterwards.
- [Guides: Upgrading from stock](https://turingpi.xyz/guides/upgrade-from-stock/): Move a Turing Pi 2 from the stock firmware to this fork, what changes on the board, and why the stock updater would downgrade you afterwards.
- [Guides: Recover a bad flash](https://turingpi.xyz/guides/recover-a-bad-flash/): Get a Turing Pi 2 BMC back after a bad firmware flash: what the board undoes by itself, and the recovery paths for when it cannot.
- [Guides: Your own certificate](https://turingpi.xyz/guides/your-own-certificate/): Install your own HTTPS certificate on the Turing Pi 2 BMC from the interface, the command line or the API, and what the board will refuse.
- [Guides: Segment the network](https://turingpi.xyz/guides/segment-the-network/): Put the compute modules and the BMC on separate VLANs using the board's own switch, and give the BMC a fixed address or leave it on DHCP.
- [Guides: Should it face the internet?](https://turingpi.xyz/guides/facing-the-internet/): Why a Turing Pi 2 BMC should not face the internet, what an exposed board gives away, and how to reach yours from outside without exposing it.
- [Guides: Monitor it](https://turingpi.xyz/guides/monitor-it/): Scrape the Turing Pi 2 BMC's own metrics into Prometheus and get a dashboard of temperature, fan, power and update history.
- [Guides: Developing](https://turingpi.xyz/guides/development/): Build this BMC firmware yourself: the container build, the override loop for working on the daemon or the interface, and what to run before a change.
- [Reference: Upstream vs this fork](https://turingpi.xyz/reference/comparison/): What upstream's Turing Pi 2 BMC firmware does and what this fork does instead, set side by side, with where each difference was measured.
- [Reference: The factory firmware](https://turingpi.xyz/reference/factory-firmware/): What shipped on a factory Turing Pi 2, how to capture it before you flash over it, and which parts of it can be republished.
- [Reference: Command line](https://turingpi.xyz/reference/cli/): Every tpi command for a Turing Pi 2: power, flash, console, firmware, the board's own address and its clock, with what each one needs.
- [Reference: Metrics](https://turingpi.xyz/reference/metrics/): Every metric the Turing Pi 2 BMC serves at /metrics in Prometheus format, what each family means, and which ones upstream never had.
- [Reference: The API](https://turingpi.xyz/reference/api/): The Turing Pi 2 BMC HTTP API: how to authenticate, the two spellings a board answers, and where the generated operation reference lives.
- [Reference: Every operation](https://turingpi.xyz/reference/api/operations/): Every operation of the Turing Pi 2 BMC HTTP API in one table: what it does, its method, its path and its group.
- [Reference: What each release's API had](https://turingpi.xyz/reference/api-history/): Which endpoints each release of the BMC daemon added, changed or removed, so you can tell what a board on older firmware is able to answer.
- [Reference: The board](https://turingpi.xyz/reference/api/board/): The board: 13 operations of the Turing Pi 2 BMC HTTP API, generated from bmcd 2.36.3's own OpenAPI document.
- [Reference: The nodes](https://turingpi.xyz/reference/api/nodes/): The nodes: 9 operations of the Turing Pi 2 BMC HTTP API, generated from bmcd 2.36.3's own OpenAPI document.
- [Reference: Firmware](https://turingpi.xyz/reference/api/firmware/): Firmware: 6 operations of the Turing Pi 2 BMC HTTP API, generated from bmcd 2.36.3's own OpenAPI document.
- [Reference: Storage](https://turingpi.xyz/reference/api/storage/): Storage: 3 operations of the Turing Pi 2 BMC HTTP API, generated from bmcd 2.36.3's own OpenAPI document.
- [Reference: Network and time](https://turingpi.xyz/reference/api/network/): Network and time: 4 operations of the Turing Pi 2 BMC HTTP API, generated from bmcd 2.36.3's own OpenAPI document.
- [Reference: Cooling and thermals](https://turingpi.xyz/reference/api/thermal/): Cooling and thermals: 3 operations of the Turing Pi 2 BMC HTTP API, generated from bmcd 2.36.3's own OpenAPI document.
- [Reference: The gate's record](https://turingpi.xyz/reference/gate-history/): Every firmware update these boards have taken and whether the gate promoted or rolled it back, read from the board's own counter.
- [Reference: What is and isn't fixed](https://turingpi.xyz/reference/known-faults/): What this fork has fixed, what is still open, and what upstream never fixed, each entry with where and when it was measured.
- [Changelogs: Every component](https://turingpi.xyz/changelog/): What changed in every release of the firmware, the daemon, the interface and the command line, from each repository's own CHANGELOG.md.

## News

- [News](https://turingpi.xyz/news/): What shipped in each Turing Pi 2 BMC firmware release and what it changed for the person using the board, newest first, with the interface pictured.
- [Two ways a board with no DNS failed to mention it](https://turingpi.xyz/news/v2.36.0/): A static address came back from every reboot with no resolvers, because the stanza that rebuilds them carried a # the board's ifup read as a comment.
- [A fixed address from the Network tab, and a clock that says why](https://turingpi.xyz/news/v2.35.0/): The BMC's own address — DHCP or static, with gateway and resolvers — from the Network tab, applied then confirmed at the new address so a typo cannot strand…
- [The switch gets VLANs, the board asks for a password, and a module is one click](https://turingpi.xyz/news/v2.34.0/): VLANs on the board's own switch, tried before they are kept; a certificate endpoint; a board still on the factory password now insists you change it before it…
- [A module armed for USB boot says so](https://turingpi.xyz/news/v2.32.0/): Pins BMC-UI 3.29.0. bmcd stays at 2.36.3 and tpi is unchanged.
- [The console stops replaying its scrollback twice](https://turingpi.xyz/news/v2.31.0/): Pins BMC-UI 3.28.0. bmcd stays at 2.36.3 and tpi is unchanged.
- [The metrics say which module is armed for USB boot](https://turingpi.xyz/news/v2.30.0/): Pins bmcd 2.36.3. BMC-UI stays at 3.27.0 and tpi is unchanged.
- [Firmware v2.29.0](https://turingpi.xyz/news/v2.29.0/): Pins bmcd 2.36.1. BMC-UI stays at 3.27.0 and tpi is unchanged.
- [Who may reach this board, from the interface that asks for the password](https://turingpi.xyz/news/v2.28.0/): Pins bmcd 2.36.0 and BMC-UI 3.27.0; tpi is unchanged and already current.
- [The latest of all three, and the SD card listed](https://turingpi.xyz/news/v2.27.0/): The first release that carries the latest of all three: BMC-UI 3.26.0, bmcd 2.34.0 and tpi 1.8.0.
- [Choose an image off the SD card](https://turingpi.xyz/news/v2.26.0/): Pins BMC-UI 3.25.0: the SD card picker, and the flash button that threw instead of flashing.
